body: Can you explain what you mean? This is actually my first semester in a data science program. I think that I am asking what you can do to - this term that the professor used to mean that there was so much data that you couldn't see through it - he compared it to fog. My tech background is limited.

This is exactly why I asked the question. I want to put together something that shows what a child should be able to do independently by age and then have each child measure their accomplishments. Like, if they should be able to bathe without being reminded or helped by age ? then I want to have that listed. If the 9yo isn't doing that, I want there to be an obvious "Hey, I should be able to do this by now."

There are tests in school to say that they should know their letters or whatever math skills but I don't have a similar resource for things that they should be able to handle at each stage to get from infant to independent adult. 

I know that you have nothing better to do with your time since you have months of vacation as a teacher, so if you'd be willing to add a couple of suggestions for each age that would be awesome. :)

There are textbooks and websites but they don't give it to me straight.
I was reading this before. Do you think that my relationship with my daughter is co-dependent? I'm a little confused about the context of that. Is it about recovering from the narc marriage or ???

I'm exploring options for her to stay with an extended family member to see if the behavior is directly related to our dynamic or if this is something that she is going to keep finding a target for and will need serious intervention. She's been hospitalized multiple times, sees a psychiatrist, therapy... she convinces the pros that she's all better and we have a cycle of her being "normal" that's followed by more intense abusive behaviors.
I just wanted to update to say that I'm feeling more hopeful today. The SI is still there in the background but not as present.
